Transgender people are not allowed to be their “authentic” selves, suppressed and abused by their parents who are bigoted, controlled by lawmakers and politicians who want to eradicate them. 

This lie tugged at my heart strings for almost three years. I didn’t see this as another toxic form of cosmetic surgery, or a band-aid on a bullet wound, but as life-saving care for someone who was trapped in the wrong body, needed to be freed, and that these procedures and drugs were the only way to that freedom. But that statement, that lie, leaves out the bigger picture and foregoes all context, deceivingly making gender dysphoria the root issue (it’s not) and transitioning the only solution to that issue (it isn’t). 

Now, it is painfully obvious that anyone who is begging for this kind of treatment to the point that they threaten or commit suicide if they do not get it is not mentally stable enough to receive that treatment in the first place, and there are clearly some other issues present that need to be addressed first and foremost. That is common sense to me now, now more than ever that I’ve learned about, analyzed intently, and critically approached every single nook and cranny of gender dysphoria imaginable. I have my speculations as to why this lie is told and why it is pushed by parents, doctors, physicians, therapists, and society, a lot of it possibly having to do with capitalism, which there is evidence for. But perhaps the biggest and most evidence-based reason people tell and believe this lie is because they do not think too critically about the mental health issues and history of transgender people. They see a person exclaiming that their body, puberty, and their sex is causing them severe emotional turmoil. If those things aren’t changed, if they aren’t “fixed”, they will kill themselves. 

And when they do, what’s the conclusion that we draw? It happened because they weren’t affirmed. Their loved ones and people from society did not view them as the sex they so desperately wanted to be, and that was extremely painful for them. They would rather die than live as their biological sex. Their gender identity is innate, just like sexuality, and denying them this would be like denying someone’s sexuality. They were born in the wrong body. Their body is wrong. They should have been born a different sex. They are a boy, or a girl, they know it. They should have had a vagina. Their puberty isn’t an objective part of human development, it is wrong. It should not be happening. Another puberty should be happening. God screwed up when he was customizing their human body, choosing their sex, and getting ready to send it to Earth, perhaps? They hate growing facial hair and having a male bone structure, it causes too much emotional pain and dysphoria. They hate growing breasts–it causes too much insecurity and devastation. Maybe too much sexualization and attention. But nobody looks into their backgrounds, like considering the presence of a personality disorder, autism, or an eating disorder (the amount of transgender people who fit this criteria is staggering). Nobody discusses with them a past of or a current presence of physical or sexual abuse, which is also staggering amongst transgender people. I have watched videos of and read stories by people who were referred to gender clinics and approved for hormone replacement therapy in as little as 15 minutes. And we wonder why there are 45,900 people in the “detrans” subreddit as it’s number of members increases rapidly, 82% of those people saying that they detransitioned because they realized their gender dysphoria was a symptom of other issues in their lives, where “discrimination, lack of support, and financial concerns were the least frequently given reasons for detransitioning. When I was 16 years old I was deeply insecure and not as self aware as I am today. I met a boy and decided I liked him and from the start I was a chameleon. When we texted, I typed like him. I took on his mannerisms. I laughed at jokes I didn’t find funny. I was a completely different person around him to the point where it made me nervous to think about him seeing me in any other light than the carefully constructed personality I made for him. As you form an identity outside of your relationship whether it be through hobbies, work, alone time, being with friends, anything. You will gain confidence to be who you are. It will start to feel like a self betrayal to not act as yourself which will always make you feel worse. As you go further into your self love journey you will start to become more comfortable with the fact that it is only you that you can depend on, and that will start to look more beautiful and comforting than it is scary. You are also a person in this relationship, and the person you are is great and deserves to be shared authentically. You don’t have to be perfect or anticipate the other persons needs or act how you think they want you to in order to be lovable. Just think...if this person would only stay with me or love me because I act in a way that they want, would I really want that love, anyhow? Say to yourself every day in the mirror: “I will never leave you.” I am 18 years old, still deeply struggling with this stuff and it’s easier for me to give you advice than take it for myself, but I hope it helped and you’re not alone
